newsitem.title: FRANCE: Turkish Dev Sol suspects on trial in France.
newsitem.headline: Turkish Dev Sol suspects on trial in France.

text.p: Eleven suspected members of the Turkish guerilla movement Dev Sol went on trial in Paris on Tuesday, accused of attacking Turkish interests in France and extorting money from Turkish businesses to finance their group.

The main suspect, Dursun Karatas, a founder of the far-left group, was being tried in absentia. Arrested in September 1994 during a routine border check, he fled France after being released on bail the following year.

His controversial release by a Paris appeals court followed threats by the group to launch further attacks on French soil and harm investigating magistrate Jean-Francois Ricard. An international warrant has been issued for his arrest.
The defendants face charges of belonging to an illegal group engaged in terrorist activities.

They are accused of damaging Turkish property in Paris, Strasbourg and Lyon between 1981 and 1992, and using intimidation to extort money from businessmen. They are also accused of entering France illegally.
One of the defendants is a German journalist, Ursula Hoppe-Unlu, who was described in court as a former member of the German leftist guerrilla movement the Red Army Faction.
A French communist-controlled journalists' union protested against her being put on trial, saying "her only crime was to have recorded the Turkish state's repression of democrats and Kurds".
Dev Sol, created in 1978, is held responsible for the deaths of several hundred people in Turkey, including the murder of then justice minister Mehmet Topac in 1994.
